funded consortium based at the
University of Maryland working on
improving the adoption of satellite
Earth observation data to better
understand agricultural food production
and supply around the world. And it has
ties back to that G20 GEO GLAM
initiative that Joe had mentioned. Which
actually sprung out of some of the food
price volatility crises from 2008 and
the 2010 era. So, I think what I really
want to highlight here is that when I'm
talking about supply we're talking about
production and yield and things like
that, but we're also talking about the
trade component of this. So, part of the
problem that we're trying to address
here is that the food system is
extremely complex. This is a very
incomplete, very messy diagram, but part
of the point is that it is messy because
there is a lot going on here. And given
that we're focused on satellite
observations, EO really is only able to
address a very small part of this very
complicated system. And what we need to
do from the NASA Harvest perspective is
start to connect those EO related
indicators to the other socioeconomic
and trade data sets that we can magnify
the impact of the data that we are
producing related to to food production.
So, thinking back to supply, we need to
consider the other parts of this chain,
not just the domestic production part,
but how do things like trade impact food
security within a country?

is to be able to give us an idea of
where we can identify what we're calling
these sort of hidden threats to hunger
based on where a country might have a
high reliance on external food sources
that
because of that reliance on input from
other countries might have these sort of
external risks to to where they are. So,
what we've done is we've started
building this platform and we've
actually put quite a lot of time into
building this platform called Harvest to
Market, which is where we try to link up
our satellite Earth Observations data to

identification step and this is work

FEWS NET, AMIS, and and many others

indicators that we can use to understand
that problem and then start to link the
data sets from there. So,
we have relationships with these
organizations both on the user side, but
also on the data producer side. So, if
you dig into this dashboard, you'll
start you'll actually see some data sets

these him- himself. And what we're
really trying to do is get all the data
in one place that we can start to make
that connection between what we see with
the satellites and how we can link that
to other parts of the hunger equation.

behind this is a project that we've been
running since 2013 called the Crop
Monitor and this is a largely EO driven
consensus-based report where every month
we're looking around the world to
understand what food supplies look like
in each country. And in places where we
have abnormal conditions, whether
they're abnormally good or abnormally
bad, we're associating those conditions
with a driver, whether that's drought,
whether that's early rains, late rains,

we take those drivers that are related
to things that are changing the
condition of the of the crop and then
associating those with um
what we call Crop Monitor events. So,
it's a moment in time snapshot of what's
really driving production in this
region.

starting from and then we're starting to
layer on all these other components,
whether that's the agrometeorological

FEWS Net warehouse,
um Harvest Stat is a statistic database

points that Vivian had brought up, um we

the thing that we can't really do is we

supply chain. Um
export bans was the example that was

from from our perspective it's better
for us to bring that data into one place
than guess at what's going to happen in
things that we really don't have a a
basis for making those guesses.

integration here. What we're doing with

crop monitor reports through uh through
rag uh into the system here, and then

information from the other data sets

collocate those in one place so you can

quick overview of what's going on in
that system, and then more importantly
who's impacted downstream.

what we're hoping to uh really bring

the data sets as well that they want to

analyze those alongside
uh their um initial query.

for me here, but I think again, you

um might be interesting for Bangladesh.
